Description: Two runs that share TMP_DIR wipe each other's status shards and crash markers. The first run exits 0, prints 'complete' and leaves a header-only tool_status.tsv.
Evidence: EXECUTED (stub tool, two concurrent stage-4 runs, WSL)
Impact: A finished run can silently carry no tool results while reporting success; a terminal run beside the window, or two non-study runs, collide.
Root cause: TMP_DIR defaults to <project>/tmp; only --study runs get their own (cli.py:1281). The in-progress marker has no pid or liveness check.
Recommendation: A unique TMP per run (or per study) and a lock file holding the pid, checked on start; stage 4 must fail if its merge finds no shards.
Test required: Two concurrent stage-4 runs on one results dir: the second refuses or uses its own TMP; the first still writes a full tool_status.tsv.

Line: webui.py:1064-1065,1281-1296; study_manage import; webui terminal route
Description: Importing a study bundle can plant an HTML file that the window serves as a report without a Content-Security-Policy; script in it can call the same-origin terminal API.
Evidence: EXECUTED hop by hop over HTTP (the browser itself was not run): import 200 -> run auto-listed -> /view served the script with no CSP -> replayed fetch to /api/terminal/run ran a command
Impact: A malicious bundle, once imported and its report opened, gives command execution as the user.
Root cause: Reports are served from the window's own origin with CSP deliberately skipped (extra={'report': True}); bundle contents are not authenticated (the manifest hash is attacker-supplied) and unlisted files are accepted.
Recommendation: Serve /view content in a sandboxed iframe or with a CSP that blocks script and connect, ideally on a separate origin; reject bundle members not in the manifest; warn on import.
Test required: A bundle with a script in its report: the served page carries a CSP that blocks it; an unlisted member makes import fail.

Description: NMI, Variation of Information and ARI are perfect (1.0, 0.0, 1.0) when a whole plasmid is missed, because the unassigned plasmid forms its own cell and the table becomes a bijection. An empty-bins tool on a plasmid-bearing isolate scores 0.0, not blank.
Evidence: EXECUTED (independently reproduced: truth p1,p2,p3; bins A->p1, B->p2; nmi 1.0000 vi 0.0000 ari 1.0000 while lw_bin_f1 0.9231, recall 0.6667)
Impact: mean_nmi, mean_variation_of_information and mean_bin_ari reward missing plasmids; docs/METHODS.md says unassigned sequence is penalised.
Root cause: Unassigned truth sequence is treated as a category of its own instead of a penalty.
Recommendation: Score NMI/VI/ARI over all truth plasmid bases with an explicit 'not binned' cluster for every unbinned base of every truth plasmid and chromosome, or withhold them and state the limitation.
Dependencies: score_bins.py, merge_bin_metrics, aggregate_results, report tables, docs/METHODS.md
Test required: Fixture above: a missed plasmid lowers NMI and ARI; empty bins is blank or defined per the docs.

Description: A gene on a contig the binner left out of its bins file is scored correct_plasmid: membership.get(query, query) turns the unbinned contig into its own singleton bin, which the matching pairs with the plasmid it covers.
Evidence: EXECUTED (metrics specialist) and READ (membership.get(query, query) at 181 and 210)
Impact: Binners that emit only plasmid bins have missed AMR genes counted as correctly placed; correct_plasmid_rate and co-localisation are inflated.
Root cause: Unbinned queries default to a bin named after themselves.
Recommendation: Treat a query absent from the bins file as unassigned for bin_matching mode; keep contig_attribution mode separate.
Dependencies: score_amr_placement.py, report AMR sections, amr_regions view
Test required: Fixture: gene on an unbinned contig is unassigned_contig, not correct_plasmid.

Description: The word-boundary regexes fail on OXFORD_NANOPORE, PACBIO_SMRT (underscore), run-together names (IlluminaMiSeq) and misspellings. 218 genuine short-read-first hybrids are labelled unknown instead of short_read_first_hybrid.
Evidence: EXECUTED (classify_method('Unicycler v0.4.7','Hybrid: Illumina and OXFORD_NANOPORE') -> unknown; the re-run over all 7,227 rows reproduces the shipped labels)
Impact: The '1,153 unknown' figure in public-v4 is inflated; strategy and polish are guesses on NCBI free text.
Root cause: Regex tokens assume spaces or punctuation around technology names.
Recommendation: Normalise tokens (split on underscore and case boundaries), add MiniSeq, and test classify_method on every distinct method/tech pair found in the cohort and lock files.
Test required: Table test over all distinct (assembly_method, tech) pairs in cohorts/public-v4.lock.json with an independently written expectation.

Description: Nine of the 1,099 'independent' (long-read-only, polish none) isolates are not independent: six name an Illumina polisher (Polypolish, Pilon) with no Illumina in the technology field, three list PacBio plus IlluminaMiSeq. They are headline-eligible.
Impact: The headline's independent-truth set contains truth polished with the benchmark's own reads; the wrong direction for a conservative rule.
Root cause: Polishers are not recognised as Illumina evidence; the strategy rule trusts the technology field.
Recommendation: Add Illumina polishers (polypolish, pilon, pypolca, polca, nextpolish, racon-with-short-reads...) as Illumina evidence; any Illumina evidence makes polish same_as_benchmark.
Test required: The count test must fail on the old labels and pass on the fixed ones; per-row expected labels for the 9.

Description: 'Runs completed' is completed/scored with no clamp: the shipped real-cohort report shows 1000% (10/1), which lifts the composite to grade A where 100% gives grade C.
Impact: The Summary headline grade can be wrong whenever scored is smaller than completed (reference-tier filter, dropped samples).
Root cause: No upper bound; denominators differ (all-tier completed vs tier-filtered scored).
Recommendation: Use the same population for numerator and denominator and clamp to 100%.
Test required: Report built from the real cohort1 data shows <=100% and the per-isolate grade agrees.

Description: 12 of 16 adapters exit 0 with an empty prediction when the tool's output is missing; the guard accepts any file in the output dir (a lone run.log); PlaScope is called outside run_adapter. The run is recorded completed with recall 0.
Evidence: EXECUTED (all 16 run against an empty dir; a dir with only run.log)
Impact: A crashed or misconfigured tool is scored as a genuine zero, not a failure; the same failure has different semantics by adapter.
Recommendation: The guard checks for the tool's real output files; adapters exit non-zero on missing output.
Test required: For each adapter: empty dir and log-only dir -> status failed with the reason 'no output'.

Description: SIGKILL (OOM, window quit) of stage 4 or the runner orphans every descendant with no status, no message and nothing in run_errors.log; Resume then offers a duplicate run on the same results folder.
Impact: Duplicate pipelines and unmerged results after a kill; the orphan keeps writing.
Root cause: No process-group kill on abnormal exit; no run lock.
Recommendation: Run in its own process group with a supervisor, write a lock with pid, make resume check the whole group.
Test required: Kill -9 the runner: no orphan survives; resume refuses while any member is alive.

Description: The heartbeat is written by the runner every 4 s and says nothing about the tool: a hung or frozen tool shows alive and running forever. There is no default timeout and no stalled, queued, waiting, retrying or completed-with-warnings state.
Impact: A stalled run cannot be told from a working one.
Root cause: Liveness is checked on the runner, not on output or CPU progress.
Recommendation: Stall detection from output growth or CPU time; a 'stalled' state; a sane default timeout per tool class.
Test required: A SIGSTOPped tool becomes stalled within the configured window.

Description: Stage 4 exits 0 when every tool failed; the run continues to the report, and the job shows done at 100%.
Impact: A run in which nothing worked ends 'done'.
Root cause: Failures are recorded per row only.
Recommendation: Exit non-zero (or 'completed with warnings') when all tools of a sample or all samples failed; surface it in the job state.
Test required: All-tools-failed run: non-zero exit and a visible state.

Description: A tool marked failed that still has score rows is not flagged; a blank metric is silently dropped (a tool's mean F1 rose from 0.626 to 0.866); a NaN is accepted and sorted as a value; a missing column crashes the report build with a raw KeyError/ValueError; the report builder has no input validation of its own and can pair stale leaderboards with new scores.
Impact: A plausible but wrong ranking from a damaged table.
Root cause: Validation covers duplicates and missing rows, not values or status/score contradictions.
Recommendation: Validate numeric columns (finite or blank), flag failed-with-score and blank-on-scored rows, and make the report builder validate its inputs.
Test required: Each mutation produces a clear error or a visible banner.

Description: The shared-sample restriction is a cliff: a tool silently absent from samples shrinks everyone's ranking set (B 0.9 vs 0.6 without it); with no overlap, each tool is ranked on its own disjoint samples and ranks are still produced.
Impact: A rank can depend on a tool's silent absence; disjoint samples are compared as if equal.
Root cause: Intersection rule with a per-tool fallback.
Recommendation: Refuse or clearly flag ranks when the shared set is small or empty; list the tools that shrink it.
Test required: Fixtures from the audit: A/B/C with and without the absent tool.

Description: Docs say all long-read-first rows are headline-eligible and four species reach 20 independent studies; under the default only long_read_only rows qualify, and only two species (E. coli 43, K. pneumoniae 30) reach 20 independent clusters.
Impact: A publication-facing claim about headline eligibility is wrong.
Root cause: Docs were written before independence was made the default.
Recommendation: Correct the docs from the computed counts and add a test that derives them.
Test required: A test computing eligible rows and species from the cohort file.

Description: 'Chromosomal contamination' is FP_bp/(true_plasmid_bp+FP_bp), not 'fraction of all truth-mapped bases'; it shows 17.1% where the score file's contamination_fraction is 0.192; the all-isolate figure is averaged over 10 samples beside an F1 from 1.
Impact: A mislabelled figure.
Recommendation: Use the stated definition or relabel.
Test required: Recompute from scores.tsv.

Description: 'Methods compared' is len(leaderboard) over the first task (1 for 4 tools); 'Leading method MOB-recon' is the only tool of its task and platon has the higher F1; 'Runs not completed 10' counts skipped baseline runs.
Impact: Headline tiles mislead.
Root cause: Counts taken from a task slice.
Recommendation: Count across tasks, say 'only tool in this task', separate skipped from failed.
Test required: Real-cohort rebuild.

Description: Table says 'validated, 1 long-read-first isolate across 3 held-out studies' while the leaderboard says '< 5 independent units'.
Impact: Contradictory validity statements.
Recommendation: One derivation.
Test required: Consistency test.

Description: Run metadata omits the PlasBench version, database versions and paths, settings and container; a local path leaks through a warning string; the tool-version filter lists tools that were not run; a demo-only sentence appears in real-data help.
Impact: Weak provenance and noise.
Recommendation: Surface manifest fields.
Test required: Report shows version and database table.

Description: circular_plasmid_recall is the share of circular truth plasmids reaching 90% coverage; recovered_complete_circular is 99.995% coverage; neither checks that the prediction is circular.
Impact: Linear fragments count as circular recovery.
Recommendation: Rename or add a circularity test.
Test required: Fixture: linear cover.

Description: AMBIGUOUS, CHIMERIC, UNPLACED and SHORT contigs are dropped from TP/FP/FN/TN, so false calls on unplaced contigs are not charged; F1 is inflated and not comparable with base-level F1.
Impact: Optimistic metric.
Recommendation: Report the dropped share beside it and never place it beside base-level F1.
Test required: Fixture with FP on unplaced.

File: ~13 FASTA readers, ~12 PAF parsers, ~50 table readers
Description: Duplicate implementations disagree: duplicate contig ids are kept-last, raised or crash by module; an empty header crashes contig_classification and make_truth; malformed PAF rows are silently dropped in the scorers; zero-length-block identity is 1.0 in build_enterprise_view and 0.0 elsewhere.
Impact: Inconsistent results from the same file.
Recommendation: Use plasbench_common readers everywhere, with one validation policy and a counted warning for dropped rows.
Test required: Fixture with duplicates, empty header, bad PAF rows.

Description: Mutation testing: CPRR boundary (>= vs >), Holm step-down and multiplier, synthetic/real refusal, secret scanning on commit and the TP clamp survive; four more are protected by a single test file.
Impact: Scientifically important lines have no protecting test.
Root cause: Tests pin outputs, not guard conditions.
Recommendation: Add boundary, numeric Holm, refusal and secret-commit tests.
Test required: Re-run the 18 mutants: all killed.

Description: About 18 tests print SKIP and exit 0 when node, minimap2, Chrome, git or results_demo is missing; a green run does not show they ran. 31 files rely on mocks; characterisation tests pin known optimism.
Impact: False confidence.
Recommendation: Count skips and print them in the runner summary; make CI fail if a required dependency is absent.
Test required: CI log lists zero unexpected skips.

Description: Commands typed into the terminal are stored verbatim in sessions.jsonl and terminal_history.jsonl (including exported keys) and can be exported to a downloadable script; settings values are masked, terminal commands are not.
Impact: Secrets at rest.
Root cause: No redaction on the terminal path.
Recommendation: Redact known key patterns before logging and exporting.
Test required: Command with a key leaves no key in the logs.

Description: The commit scanner misses password: in .yml, ZENODO_TOKEN= in .cfg and NCBI_API_KEY= in a file named config.local, and never scans files over 1 MB or with other suffixes.
Impact: A secret can be committed.
Root cause: Suffix list and generic regex too narrow.
Recommendation: Scan all text files under a size cap with a broader pattern set.
Test required: Fixtures for the three misses.

Description: Several downloads have no mandatory checksum (Platon DB optional, PLSDB warn-only, MOB-suite none, gplas2 tarball by commit); release checksums come from the same host.
Impact: Supply-chain exposure.
Recommendation: Pin hashes in the registry and refuse without them.
Test required: Installer fails on a wrong hash.

Description: truth_technology and truth_assembly_strategy disagree on 101 rows (66 long_read vs long_read_first_hybrid, 32 long_read vs short_read_first_hybrid, 3 hybrid vs long_read_only); no code reconciles them.
Impact: Contradictory cohort labels.
Recommendation: Reconcile and flag.
Test required: Consistency check in validate-cohort.

Description: All 7,227 rows are curation grade B, so Tier 1 and grade A are unreachable; the tier-1 population is empty and 'primary' is tier-2 independent.
Impact: Docs describe Tier 1 as the gold standard on a cohort that cannot have one.
Recommendation: State this in the report and docs.
Test required: Report banner.

Description: identity_valid returns True when a sample has no provenance record, applying identity criteria with unknown polish (contradicts 'unknown never assumed independent'); sheet_limit.independent_truth_only ignores curation tier C.
Impact: Rare mislabel.
Recommendation: Default False.
Test required: Fixture without provenance.

Description: Stage 8 checks only that pred_<tool>.plasmid.fasta is non-empty; an uninstalled tool is 'skipped' and an older prediction left in place passes.
Impact: A recommendation can use a stale prediction.
Recommendation: Delete or version predictions per run.
Test required: Stale-prediction fixture.

Description: Retries re-run the same command into the same output directory without cleanup (tools that refuse an existing --outdir fail on the retry).
Impact: A retry may fail for the wrong reason.
Recommendation: Clean or use a per-attempt directory.
Test required: Retry with a directory-refusing stub.

Description: Uses one global THREADS for every tool, so thread-seconds and CPU utilisation are wrong when per-tool threads differ; MEMORY_GB is not divided by parallel jobs; oversubscription is only advised and absent in stages 6-8.
Impact: Wrong efficiency figures.
Recommendation: Record threads per run.
Test required: Per-tool thread fixture.

Description: Only stage 4 (runtime, peak RSS) and stage 3 (runtime) are measured; stages 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8 record no timing; stage-4 runtime includes all retries and peak RSS comes from the last attempt and is blank on timeout or without /usr/bin/time; no hard free-space check before downloads.
Impact: Resource claims cannot be backed.
Recommendation: Time every stage and each attempt; add a disk check.
Test required: Stage timing table in the run.

Description: Download size (0.615 bytes/base, 12.1 MB per reference) and PLASMER_MEMORY_GB=32 are hardcoded; README timings (30-60 min per isolate, 1-3 hours, 30-90 min install) are estimates; PERFORMANCE_AUDIT figures depend on workload and machine.
Impact: Estimates read as measurements.
Recommendation: Run the measured pilot.
Test required: Pilot table.

Description: score_failures.tsv reasons are only 'see <log>'; malformed FASTA is caught at stage 5, not stage 4; no database pre-flight so every sample x retry launches; direct stage 4/5 accept an empty cohort and stage 6 then blames stage 5.
Impact: Poor diagnostics.
Recommendation: Put the reason in the table; pre-flight checks.

Description: The compression-ratio check runs only above 50 MB and the cap is 8 GiB, so a low-ratio bomb below 8 GiB is accepted.
Impact: Disk exhaustion.
Recommendation: Lower the cap and check free space.
Test required: Large low-ratio zip.

Description: Windows reserved names (CON) and a trailing dot (foo. aliases foo) are accepted as study names.
Impact: Aliased or unusable folders on Windows.
Recommendation: Reject reserved names and trailing dots.
Test required: Names test.

Description: config/local.env (holding the NCBI key) is written with the default umask; some scripts send the NCBI key in URL query strings.
Impact: Key exposure.
Recommendation: chmod 600; send keys in headers.

Description: Backend routes with no UI control: git/show, runs/forget (a registered results folder cannot be removed from the Runs list), git remote_remove, gh_setup_git, gh_create.
Impact: Functionality unreachable from the window.
Recommendation: Add controls or remove.

Description: Two validate calls have no catch (Start/Run keep their previous state on a network error); ~30 empty catch blocks leave stale panels with no message; clipboard Copy buttons toast success without awaiting the write.
Impact: Silent UI failures.
Recommendation: Show an error line and keep controls consistent.

Description: Three overlapping terms (Reconstruction, Binning, reassembly) are used for related concepts; the Tools page shows 'binning reconstruction' with no inline explanation; a leaderboard rank cannot be interpreted without the guide; failures after a run show 'done' at exit 0 with developer-style errors; results and leaderboards have no export control.
Impact: A new user cannot tell what a rank means or why a run failed.
Recommendation: One vocabulary, inline help, an export button.
Test required: Usability walkthrough.

Description: Stale counts: '23 tools and three baselines' (20 real tools + 3 baselines + 5 demo stand-ins), 58 CLI subcommands (54), 174 modules (183), '27 tools'; config.sh comments say '(proposed)' for locked decisions; HEADLINE_MAX_REFERENCE_TIER is exported twice; HEADLINE_REFERENCE_INDEPENDENCE is a legacy duplicate of HEADLINE_INDEPENDENCE.
Impact: Documentation drift.
Recommendation: Generate counts from the registry.
Test required: Consistency test.

Function: format_rate, current_block, container_of, tab_of, is_legacy, is_signal, wsl_available; GPLAS_THREADS
Description: Seven functions have no caller and GPLAS_THREADS (exported) has no effect on gplas.
Impact: Dead code and a no-op setting.
Recommendation: Remove or wire.

Description: 40 of 76 subprocess calls pass no timeout (minimap2, mash, seqtk helpers).
Impact: A hung helper hangs the stage.
Recommendation: Add timeouts.

Description: False-confidence tests: the count test pins 1,099 (a correct fix lowers it); the ledger test passes if a symbol is on the cited line whatever it does; the adversarial test pins known optimism; classify_method is tested on hand-written strings, not the cohort's real tokens.
Impact: Tests enforce the defects.
Recommendation: Replace with derived expectations.

Description: Only mob_recon, platon and plasmidSPAdes have real-binary checks (one 4.3 kb plasmid, weekly, advisory); 13 tools are tested only against stand-ins; the registry points to test/real_tools/records/ which does not exist; 7 installers are 'planned'.
Impact: Most adapters are unverified against the real software.
Recommendation: Run each real tool on a small fixture in CI or a scheduled job and record outputs.
Test required: Scheduled job per tool.

Description: Gene recovery differs between scorers: placement takes the single best interval, the base scorer takes the union (a gene split 0-48 + 52-100 is 1.0 vs not_recovered).
Impact: Inconsistent AMR numbers.
Recommendation: One definition.

Description: No bins gives P = R = 0.0 where the base scorer's precision is blank; the bin scorer keeps secondary alignment rows and does not check target lengths (user-supplied PAF only).
Impact: Inconsistent undefined handling.
Recommendation: Align the rules.

Description: scores.tsv is truncated in place then appended: a kill mid-merge leaves a partial file.
Impact: Partial table.
Recommendation: Write to a temp file and rename.

Description: ci.yml has no top-level permissions block; actions are pinned by tag not SHA; release.yml holds contents:write and packages:write.
Impact: Supply-chain hardening.
Recommendation: Pin and minimise permissions.

Description: Marker-free plasmids are dropped from truth using PlasmidFinder and MOB-typer evidence, the same databases baseline_replicon and mob_recon use, so replicon-based tools are favoured by construction.
Impact: Circular evidence for some tools (disclosed in METHODS).
Recommendation: Report with and without the exclusion.

Description: The cluster-t interval is not clamped (0.498 to 1.102 for a proportion) and constant data gives a zero-width interval; nominal 95% intervals under-cover in several designs (documented).
Impact: Intervals outside the metric's range.
Recommendation: Clamp or use a bounded method.

Description: The shipped real-cohort report is 18 MB, was built with 0.2.3 (stale against main: a rebuild gives a cautious headline), ranks on 1 isolate of 10, has a dangling #enterprise anchor and 3,050 of 3,104 relative file links that do not exist in the checkout.
Impact: A stale artefact that can be mistaken for a result.
Recommendation: Rebuild with current main or mark clearly as an example.
